facts.raw_span: A 19-month-old boy was brought to the emergency department after an episode of reduced consciousness while bathing
he turned blue around the lips and began gasping for air
his eyes “rolled back,” and he did not interact with his parents
There were no clonic movements, and he did not respond to physical stimulation
he fell asleep for approximately 1 hour
On arrival, he was alert and appeared well
There were no focal findings on examination
his development was appropriate
laboratory studies—including a blood glucose level of 5.5 mmol/L—were normal
An electrocardiogram demonstrated sinus rhythm with a normal QT interval
Bathing in lukewarm water while his vital signs were monitored provoked hypotonia, tachycardia, and brief apnea with associated desaturation
The first interictal EEG was normal using the standard 10–20 system
